idiom_name: owner + property list (indicator -> value) + descriptors + named access API
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: the owner hides a name-to-value container behind get/set/has/remove/enumerate; the container is the property list and the names are the indicators. Keep the schema separate - a descriptor table (type, default, constraints, mandatory, per-type allowed set) is what turns a bag of values into a checked model, and it is also what lets tools discover the state. Decide the absence contract explicitly (absent vs null) and the key identity (strings for flexibility, immutable key objects where type checking matters), keep fixed mandatory attributes as ordinary fields, and let dynamic member syntax in any language delegate to this one API instead of becoming a second pathway.
code_sketch:
owner:
    props = {}                         # property list: indicator -> value
    set(name, value): validate(name, value); props[name] = value
    get(name) -> value or ABSENT       # absence is a first-class answer
    has(name), remove(name)
    names() -> props.keys()            # discoverability for tools and serializers
descriptors: name -> {type, default, constraints, mandatory}   # checked on write
read: value = get(name); if ABSENT: apply the descriptor default or fail explicitly
pitfalls: Skipping the descriptor/schema layer: without it, validity lives in every client and discovery is impossible.
Putting the whole domain model into property bags instead of only the genuinely dynamic remainder.
Sharing one container between instances (or using globals) instead of per-instance state.

Wrong move: Treating Qt dynamic properties as a replacement for Q_PROPERTY -> type-safe metadata, tooling and compatibility checks fail -> instead keep stable contract fields as Q_PROPERTY and reserve dynamic properties for genuinely open metadata.

Wrong move: Using g_object_set_data() as a validated domain-property schema -> untyped pointers, caller-owned lifetimes and NULL ambiguity undermine invariants -> instead use bounded keys plus descriptors or typed storage, and keep keyed data for auxiliary associations.

Wrong move: Copying untrusted request keys into a JavaScript object with Object.assign or deep merge -> mass assignment or prototype pollution can modify privileged or inherited state -> instead allow-list keys, reject prototype-control names and bind through DTO/schema validation.
